test_description: Verify that context-writer boundary enforcement text is accurate: it must not claim the framework respects a boundary that compile-time code violates. The test reads the generated repair context and asserts no false claims about journal immutability at compile time.
test_assertions: Context-writer boundary text does not claim journal files are never read at compile time
Context-writer boundary text still instructs users not to edit journal files
Boundary text acknowledges that journal files are runtime artifacts managed by the framework
change_description: Update the boundary enforcement text at line 198 to stop claiming the framework never reads journal files. The observe phase found evidence that compile-time code reads journal manifest (run/index.ts:1243) and runstate (run/index.ts:968), making the current text self-contradicting. Replace with accurate text: journal files are runtime artifacts managed by the framework, users must not edit them, and any compile-time reads from journal are tracked exceptions.
why_this_correction: The observe phase evidence (findings.json lines 48-49) proves the framework enforces a boundary it does not itself respect: context-writer.ts:198 tells users journal files are READ-ONLY while run/index.ts:1243 reads journal manifest as a compilation fallback. This self-contradiction erodes trust in the framework's guidance and causes downstream confusion about what the boundary actually is. Fixing the text to be accurate has high leverage because it prevents every future developer from being misled by the false claim.
